content.title: Table 11: Categorization of risk factors for venous thromboembolism based on the risk of recurrence over the long-term

table_summary.purpose: Classify index VTE/PE risk factors by estimated long-term recurrence risk

risk_categories.description: Major transient or reversible factors associated with >10-fold increased risk for the index VTE event (compared to patients without the risk factor)
examples: Surgery with general anaesthesia for >30 min
Confined to bed in hospital (only 'bathroom privileges') for ≥3 days due to an acute illness or acute exacerbation of a chronic illness

risk_categories.description: Transient or reversible factors associated with ≤10-fold increased risk for first (index) VTE; also non-malignant persistent risk factors and cases with no identifiable risk factor
examples: Admission to hospital for <3 days with an acute illness
Confined to bed out of hospital for ≥3 days with an acute illness
Leg injury (without fracture) associated with reduced mobility for ≥3 days
Inflammatory bowel disease (listed as a non-malignant persistent risk factor)
Active autoimmune disease (listed as a non-malignant persistent risk factor)

risk_categories.description: Persistent major risk factors associated with high recurrence risk
examples: One or more previous episodes of VTE in the absence of a major transient or reversible factor

footnotes_and_notes.a: If anticoagulation is discontinued after the first 3 months (based on data from Baglin et al. and Iorio et al.).
footnotes_and_notes.b: Categorization of risk factors for the index VTE event is in line with that proposed by the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH). The present Guidelines avoid certain terms (text truncated on page).

sources_cited_on_page: International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH)
